title: ARIA issuer key set, as published at /v1/keyset (draft)
description: Every key an issuer has signed credentials with, in the order they became active, append-only: the first is the anchor, whose fingerprint the publisher fixes when the set is first published and keeps apart from it; each later key is introduced by a composite signature of the key before it, which also covers that earlier entry in full; only the last is active. A verifier trusts the key whose fingerprint it pinned out of band; being listed here grants no trust. Draft: the published values are decision D2, TLF's.
$comment: Rules JSON Schema cannot express, checked by the publishing authority (conformance/vectors/keyset.json): keys are ordered by active_from and their windows follow one another; the first key's fingerprint is the publisher's configured anchor; introduced_by names the key before it and its signature verifies, both halves, under that key over the canonical JSON of {ctx: 'aria-keyset-introduction-v1', key_id, suite, public_key_mldsa65, public_key_ed25519, active_from, previous}, previous being the entry before it (key_id, suite, both keys, active_from, active_until), so dropping, replacing or rewriting an accepted entry fails; key_id fragments use letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', and timestamps are YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ; fingerprint is 'sha256:' and the hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of {key_id, suite, public_key_mldsa65, public_key_ed25519}; the Ed25519 key is canonical, of large order and torsion-free.

key_id.description: The verification method credentials name in proof.verificationMethod: the issuer DID and a fragment.

active_until.description: Null while the key is active. Set on retirement; the key stays listed, since credentials it signed are never re-signed.
